key_insight: Simple graph-dependent IQP and QAOA circuits can encode enough structure to distinguish many non-isomorphic graphs, and in some settings even reconstruct the underlying graph from samples.
engineering_relevance: This suggests quantum circuit outputs may provide practical graph fingerprints for symmetry detection, benchmarking, and potentially new approaches to graph-isomorphism-related subroutines.
method: Design graph-dependent IQP and QAOA circuits.
Use Hamming weight distributions and ZZ-correlator matrices as graph invariants.
For IQP, analyze probability multiplicities within Hamming-weight sectors; derive exact characterizations at specific angles.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show QAOA depth p=2 distinguishes all 10,486 cospectral regular graph pairs tested up to 18 vertices, and the IQP invariant distinguishes every non-isomorphic graph pair tested.
watch_item: The results are largely numerical and structural, so it remains unclear whether these distinctions can be extracted efficiently for general graph isomorphism at scale.
paper_title: Testing graph isomorphism using simple quantum circuits
